content:
Katie Zacharia, whose blink-and-you’d-miss-it tenure as White House press secretary lasted just five days in October, raised eyebrows with her promotion of first lady Melania Trump’s upcoming documentary series.

Zacharia on Sunday shared a black-and-white photo of herself posing in front of a curtain. Beneath the image were the title of the “Melania” documentary film, its January release date and the Amazon MGM Studios logo. She used the post to plug the Nov. 20 release of “Melania: The Series,” the follow-up to the movie.

Critics quickly questioned the choice of image.

“Using a picture of yourself for a series about someone else is just incredible content,” one commenter wrote.

She subsequently appeared to delete the post.

When the progressive MeidasTouch Network flagged the apparent deletion and shared a screenshot, Zacharia again defended herself.

She wrote: “For the record, this was used at the initial Premiere in January as a way to promote the film — this was taken at the Kennedy Center to spread the word about the film. You can find many such photos of those who attended. You’re welcome.”
